title: Tilted lens: candidate Noor Malik
content:
Quick sketch / brain dump after loop with Noor Malik (senior runtime engineer candidate). Filling this in before details fade — rough, chronological, and opinionated. Use as a handoff for hiring committee and for my own follow-up asks.

Context:
- Loop format: 90m — 30m pairing (latency-sensitive batching patch), 30m system-design + rollout discussion, 30m behavioral & team fit.
- Interviewers: Anais (scheduling), Maya (pairing), Rachit (system design).
- Candidate background: 7 years infra/ML systems, last at an infra startup; shipped quantized model serving in prod, did GPU kernel perf work a couple years ago.

Raw impressions (first 15 minutes after):
- Bright, rapid clarifier. Good instincts on tradeoffs (latency vs throughput, model quality vs cost).
- Pragmatic: prefers incremental improvements and observability-first changes rather than big-bang rewrites.
- Slightly defensive on past design decisions; some stories framed as tradeoff-limited rather than technical oversight.

Pairing exercise notes (Maya's notes + mine):
- Task: modify a minibatching scheduler to favor latency for short requests while maintaining throughput for long-horizon workloads.
- Approach: Noor first sketched a two-queue scheduler with adaptive timeouts and token-based prioritization. Good callout on starvation for large batches and clear fallback policy.
- Concrete patch: wrote a small change to preempt batch assembly when high-priority requests present; implemented a soft-deadline heuristic. Code was readable, tests minimal but present.
- Missed: didn't immediately call out importance of end-to-end metrics we should track (p95 latency broken out by route, queue size distribution, effective throughput per worker). Prompted them and they recovered.
- Edge-case thinking: did not consider hot-path route isolation (single tenant spiky traffic) until asked. Their follow-ups were reasonable.

System design / rollout discussion (my half):
- Topic: rolling out quantized model variant behind canary; maintain accuracy guardrails.
- Positives: solid rollout plan — canary traffic split, shadow eval, automated rollback triggers tied to eval metrics. Like that they tied to a small fixed prompt suite for metric stability and suggested periodic refresh.
- Concerns: suggested client-side fallbacks as a last-resort but did not strongly advocate for server-side fail-open for critical routes; I probed and they agreed it warrants policy conversation.
- Observability: proposed per-request metadata tagging (model-version, quantization-level), which fits our telemetry patterns.

Behavioral / culture fit:
- Communication: clear, favors diagrams, balances technical depth with product impact.
- Collaboration: described examples of cross-team friction and how they mediated by shipping a shim + monitoring to prove value — good sign of pragmatic influence.
- Growth areas: less experience advocating for infra budget at exec level; may need coaching on elevating metrics into economic terms.

Strengths (short):
- Strong practical systems instincts for latency-sensitive schedulers.
- Good testable rollout thinking for model variants and quantization.
- Code hygiene and readable patches under pairing pressure.

Risks / red flags (short):
- Limited exposure to HSM/KMS integrations (we asked; has peripheral knowledge but not hands-on). Could be mitigated by pairing with security lead.
- Slight tendency to optimize for local correctness before considering global policy (e.g., tenancy isolation). Not a dealbreaker but needs wider-scope prompts.
- Communication: can be defensive when their decisions are probed — felt like a reflex to justify rather than explore. It calmed once we set collaborative framing.

Quick proprietary rubric (my internal scoring):
- Technical breadth (kernels/serving/runtime): 7/10
- System design+rollout: 8/10
- Code & pairing: 8/10
- Cross-team influence: 6/10
- Overall recommended level: Senior (IC4) with potential for IC5 with mentoring in exec-level framing and security integrations.

Follow-ups I want before final committee: (keep short)
1) Ask them for a one-page postmortem of a past perf regression they owned: timeline, metrics, and how they validated the fix. Look for concrete telemetry and owner handoffs. (Due: 48h)
2) Quick async question about KMS/HSM: describe a concrete flow (key wrapping/unwrapping) they would use to decrypt model weights at load time in a private deployment. Gauge practical surface vs theoretical.
3) Expand on tenancy isolation thought: given noisy neighbor scenario, how would they prioritize rate-limits vs route-level replica allocation? One-paragraph answer.

Suggested hire note to add to packet (one-liner):
- "Noor Malik — Senior Runtime Engineer candidate. Strong latency-first system designer with pragmatic rollout instincts. Recommended hire at Senior level; needs brief ramp on security integrations and exec-facing cost articulation."

Misc scratch (questions I liked that they asked):
- "How do you prioritize accuracy regression alerts vs latency SLO breaches in production?" (good product + infra joint thinking)
- Asked about our customer mix for private deployments and regulatory constraints — shows they are thinking beyond code.

My decision stance: Positive lean. Would hire for a Senior IC slot today and plan a 3-month ramp focusing on (1) security/KMS pairings, (2) cross-team budgeting narratives, (3) observability ownership for a route.

Notes to self for committee: include Maya/Anais quick thumbs and ask for any hard blocker on KMS background. If any dissent, push for a short reference call focused on security/integration work.

End.
